key_insight: Interference between light’s electric and magnetic dipole interactions can generate spin and charge photocurrents even in inversion-symmetric crystals.
engineering_relevance: This mechanism could broaden photovoltaic and optoelectronic material options to centrosymmetric crystals such as cubic silicon and SrTiO3.
method: Develop a unified microscopic theory of electric–magnetic dipole interference.
Combine symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations.
Separate shift-like and injection-like currents and classify symmetry and polarization dependence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports calculated responses that scale linearly with light intensity and are roughly 10^-3–10^-2 as strong as conventional non-centrosymmetric responses, yet predicted to be experimentally accessible.
watch_item: The weaker response requires sensitive experimental validation; the abstract reports neither solar-cell performance nor an AI component.
paper_title: Spin and Charge Photocurrents from Electric-Magnetic Dipole Interference in Centrosymmetric Crystals
